parts.title: Renting an apartment
parts.transcript: Part 1: an accommodation agent describes an apartment to Jessica, who will rent in central Sydney. It's a studio (~34 sq m), shares a laundry, on the 14th floor, with harbour views and a balcony. Tenants get a free gym, an indoor pool, two cinemas (reduced rate), underground parking and good transport. Rent $580/month including electricity. Available from the 13th of August.

parts.transcript: Part 2: a driving-school employee explains two courses (theory + practical). Theory flow: Lessons (classroom/online) -> Revision in the classroom (11=E) + a practice Trial test (12=I) -> RTD test -> Provisional licence (13=C). Practical flow: Circuit-based training & assessment (14=B) -> training on the highways -> Trial test -> RTD test (15=H) -> Full driving licence then 12 months' probation (16=A). Q17 B (details on website, no booking), Q18 A (classes in several languages), Q19 C (book at kiosks in big stores), Q20 B (no penalty if you give 72 hours' notice; medical certificate not accepted).

parts.transcript: Part 4: a student presents on earth-sheltered (underground) housing. Advantages: low impact on the environment (31); greater use of alternative energy-efficient technologies (32); very long lifespan (33, 500+ years); easy to maintain; no noise from traffic outside (34); health benefits from advanced ventilation methods (35, helps asthma). In the UK: easier to get planning permission, especially in conservation areas (36); may replace coastal mobile homes. Two projects: favourable reaction - both Mole Manor (media/most desirable) and Hockerton (awards) (37=C); self-sufficiency in energy - Hockerton (38=B); low building costs - Hockerton (39=B, £80,000 each); luxurious accommodation - Mole Manor (40=A, grandeur, worth £800,000+).
